question: Which of the following languages was not included in the 8th schedule of Indian Constitution through the 92nd amendment act?A. MaithiliB. BodoC. SanthaliD. Kannada (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 3)
options: A
D
C
B
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kannada

Explanation:
The 92nd Amendment Act (2003) added four new languages to the 8th Schedule of the Indian Constitution: Maithili, Bodo, Santhali, and Dogri. Kannada was already included in the 8th Schedule since the original constitution and thus was not added through this amendment. Prior to the 92nd amendment, the 8th Schedule contained 18 languages; after the amendment, it increased to 22 languages. The 8th Schedule currently recognizes 22 official languages. The 92nd amendment was significant in recognizing the linguistic diversity of India, especially languages from the northeastern and eastern regions. Note that the 92nd amendment is sometimes called the 91st amendment in some older documents, but it is officially the 92nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.

☛ Total languages in 8th Schedule currently → 22
☛ Dravidian languages already in 8th Schedule → Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam
☛ Year of 92nd Amendment → 2003
☛ Which language was added by 21st Amendment (1967) → Sindhi
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी भाषा 92 वें संशोधन अधिनियम के माध्यम से भारतीय संविधान की 8 वीं अनुसूची में शामिल नहीं की गई थी?A. मैथिलीB. बोडोC. संथालीD. कन्नड़ (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 3)

question: Which of the following statements is not true?A. The Constitution says that the Chief Minister shall be appointed by the Chief justice of the High Court.B. The governor elects only those people as ministers, who have been nominated by the Chief Minister.C. The Chief Minister is the chairman of a state’s Planning BoardD. The governor of a state cannot dismiss a Chief Minister as long as the CM receives the support of the majority in Vidhan Sabha(state’s Lower House) (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 3)
options: B
D
A
C
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Statement A

Explanation:
According to Article 164 of the Indian Constitution, the Governor appoints the Chief Minister, not the Chief Justice of the High Court. The Chief Minister is the leader of the majority party in the state legislative assembly. Statement B is true because the Governor appoints ministers on the advice of the Chief Minister. Statement C is correct as the Chief Minister is the chairman of the State Planning Board. Statement D is true since the Governor cannot dismiss the Chief Minister as long as he enjoys the majority support in the Vidhan Sabha. Hence, only statement A is false.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who appoints the Chief Minister? → Governor
☛ Who is the chairman of the State Planning Board? → Chief Minister
☛ On whose advice are ministers appointed? → Chief Minister
☛ When can the Governor dismiss the Chief Minister? → When he loses majority in the assembly
☛ Article 164 deals with? → Appointment of Chief Minister

question: Name the committee appointed by Rajiv Gandhi in 1986 on "Revitalization of Panchayati Raj Institutions for Democracy and Development".A) Ashok Mehta Committee.B) L.M. Singhvi Committee.C) G.V.K. Rao Committee.D) Balwant Rai Mehta Committee. (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 3)

Singhvi Committee recommended constitutional status for Panchayati Raj, which later formed the basis of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992). question: In the Parliament of India, who was the first speaker of the Lok Sabha?A. M.A AyyangarB. Ganesh MavalankarC. Sardar Hukam SinghD. Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy (RRB NTPC Tier I (28/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: C
B
A
D
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ganesh Mavalankar

Explanation:
Ganesh Mavalankar was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha in the Indian Parliament. He served from 15 May 1952 to 27 February 1956. He was popularly known as 'Dada' and was a freedom fighter and politician from Gujarat. The Lok Sabha was constituted for the first time after the general elections held in 1952. M.A. Ayyangar became the second Speaker, while Sardar Hukam Singh and Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy served as Speakers later.

☛ By what name was Ganesh Mavalankar known? → Dada
☛ In which year was Lok Sabha constituted? → 1952

question: Why is it remarked that the “pocket of the Indian President is bigger than that of the American President” in reference to Pocket Vetro Power of the president?A. The power of the Indian President not to take any action (either positive or negative) on the bill for an indefinite period.B. The President of the USA has to return the bill for reconsideration within 10 days, as against 30 days for the Indian President.C. The President of the USA has to return the bill for reconsideration within 10 days, as against 20 days for the Indian President.D. The President of the USA can't return the bill for reconsideration if he kept it for more than 10 days, while that is not the case with the Indian President. (RRB NTPC Tier I (29/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: D
B
C
A
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A

Explanation:
The remark that the "pocket of the Indian President is bigger than that of the American President" refers to the pocket veto power. In India, under Article 111, the President can withhold assent, return the bill for reconsideration, or take no action, effectively killing the bill indefinitely without any time limit. This is known as a pocket veto. In the USA, the President also has a pocket veto, but it applies only when Congress is adjourned within 10 days of presenting the bill. If Congress is in session, the bill automatically becomes law after 10 days if not signed. Hence, the Indian President's pocket veto is absolute, giving him more power to block legislation, while the American President's power is limited by congressional sessions. Thus, the Indian President's 'pocket' is bigger.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Type of veto power of Indian President → Suspensive veto
☛ When does US President's pocket veto apply? → When Congress is adjourned
☛ Time limit for Indian President to act on a bill → No limit

question: The GST Bill introduced in parliament in 2015 isA. A financial bill.B. Not a money bill.C. A constitutional amendment bill.D. An ordinary bill. (RRB NTPC Tier I (29/03/2016) Shift 3)
options: A

B

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is C

Explanation:
The GST Bill introduced in Parliament in 2015 was a Constitutional Amendment Bill because it required amendments to Article 246A and other provisions of the Constitution. It was passed as the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act. The bill was brought to implement the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India. It was neither a money bill, nor a financial bill, nor an ordinary bill. GST is an indirect tax that subsumes various taxes levied by central and state governments. After the constitutional amendment, the GST Council was formed.

question: Which country has the longest written constitution in the world? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/01/2021) Shift 2)

solution:

question: In a parliamentary system, the legislative, judicial and emergency powers are in reality used by the President only on the advice of the_______. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Council of Ministers
Chief Minister
Members of the Parliament
Vice President
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Council of Ministers

Explanation:
In the Indian parliamentary system, the President is the constitutional head of the state, but the real executive power lies with the Council of Ministers. The President exercises legislative, judicial, and emergency powers only on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister. Article 74 of the Indian Constitution provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at its head to aid and advise the President. The President cannot reject the advice of the Council; he can only send it back for reconsideration. If the Council reiterates its advice, the President is bound to accept it. Thus, all powers—legislative, judicial (e.g., pardoning power), and emergency powers—are effectively exercised by the Council of Ministers.

question: In India, all the bills introduced and passed by both the houses (Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha) can come into force only after they receive the assent of:  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: President
Parliament
Supreme Court
Prime Minister
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is President

Explanation:
According to Article 111 of the Indian Constitution, any bill passed by both Houses of Parliament cannot become law without the President's assent. The President has three options: he may give assent, withhold assent (pocket veto), or return the bill for reconsideration (except for Money Bills). This process ensures a separation of powers between the executive and legislature. Only after the President's assent does the bill become an Act and come into force in the country.

question: According to India's Election Commission, political parties cannot release their manifesto in pre poll silence period of: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/01/2021) Shift 1)

1 जनवरी

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है 1 जनवरी

Explanation:
नीति आयोग (राष्ट्रीय भारत परिवर्तन संस्थान) का गठन 1 जनवरी 2015 को किया गया था, जिसने योजना आयोग का स्थान लिया। यह भारत सरकार का एक प्रमुख नीति थिंक टैंक है जो सरकार को रणनीतिक और तकनीकी सलाह प्रदान करता है। योजना आयोग की स्थापना 1950 में हुई थी, जबकि नीति आयोग का गठन प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी के नेतृत्व में किया गया। नीति आयोग का मुख्य उद्देश्य सहकारी संघवाद को बढ़ावा देना और राज्यों को नीति निर्माण में भागीदार बनाना है। इसके पहले अध्यक्ष प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी थे। नीति आयोग में एक गवर्निंग काउंसिल, क्षेत्रीय परिषदें और विभिन्न विशेषज्ञ समूह शामिल हैं।
